finding.why: None of these three multi-row writers is wrapped in `db.transaction()`. If the app is killed/backgrounded mid-loop (routine on mobile), the row set is left partially written. The clearest user-visible case: track_learning_order_dao.upsertOrder is called from saveSedarimOrder/saveMasechtosOrder (lib/features/tracks/track_order/data/repositories/track_learning_order_repository_impl.dart) with the full reordered item list — tens of refs for a masechtos reorder. A crash partway through leaves some refs at their new sortOrder and others at stale values, silently scrambling the track's learning order with no error surfaced. point_config_dao.seedDefaults has a similar exposure (a stage left with no PointConfig row); study_day_config_dao.seedDefaults is lower-risk because isStudyDay() defaults a missing row to 'study' anyway.
finding.recommendation: Wrap each loop body in `await db.transaction(() async { ... })` so the whole seed/reorder either fully applies or fully rolls back.
acceptance_criteria: seedDefaults (both DAOs) and upsertOrder execute inside db.transaction().
A regression test forces a failure on a middle iteration (e.g. a duplicate/invalid row) and asserts none of the batch's rows persisted (all-or-nothing).
